supersedes: The 2026-08-27T20:45Z revision of this file. Two numbers in it were wrong; see corrections_to_previous_revision.

premise_correction.audit_claimed: 78 of 360 mutating actions had vendor read-back (~22%); 282 rested on accepted_async.
premise_correction.actually_found: The 78 were catalog DECLARATIONS. Only 3 executed at runtime — schedule_write_success_verification returned early for every non-membership action, so the 75 follow_up_entity_get declarations were inert.

live_vendor_proof.org: f07e57c0-1501-4000-8000-c04e57a00001 (isolated smoke org, not a customer org)
live_vendor_proof.negative_control: fabricated id 99178939302488 refused with follow_up_read_returned_no_entity — the read genuinely discriminates and the positive is not vacuous
live_vendor_proof.cleanup: test contact deleted, smoke org left clean

bug_found_only_by_live_testing.summary: The adapter shipped broken in b7776ba4 and every entity_get read returned unverified.
bug_found_only_by_live_testing.cause: extract_entity_id searched a fixed envelope key list (data/structured/result/record/entity/object). HubSpot nests the record under its own resource name — {"contact": {"id": ...}} — so the id was present in a successful read and the adapter could not see it.
bug_found_only_by_live_testing.why_tests_missed_it: Every unit test mocked a flat {"id": ...} response. The mocks encoded the same wrong assumption as the code.
bug_found_only_by_live_testing.blast_radius: Fail-honest, not false-positive: affected writes stayed accepted_async. No write was ever labelled verified on a failed read.
bug_found_only_by_live_testing.fix: Walk the response shallowest-first, and confirm by matching the KNOWN written id rather than picking 'the' id out of the payload, so a neighbouring nested id cannot produce a false confirmation.

delivered.alias_bug_fixed: The executability gate checked raw registry membership while invoke_tool resolves aliases first, so 5 Google reads (google_drive.files.get -> drive.files.get) were rejected as unregistered despite executing fine.
delivered.honesty_fix: accepted_async set verified=True, so an unproven write earned the green 'Verified' pill and the verified lifecycle state, with 'completion is not yet proven' demoted to a collapsed detail line. Split into three states; a vendor ack now reads 'Accepted — not yet confirmed'. Mutation-proven.

corrections_to_previous_revision.claimed: 71 accepted_async actions have a directly executable GET sibling, 54 of them straightforward to wire, reaching ~36.7%.
corrections_to_previous_revision.actual: 0. Every action with a same-resource GET sibling was already declared among the 75. The 71 was produced by a crude candidate heuristic and does not survive inspection.
detail: 0 remaining accepted_async actions are creates with a same-resource GET sibling.

28 have a same-resource GET but are state changes (campaigns.pause, issues.transition, deals.update_stage, incidents.resolve). Reading the id back proves the entity EXISTS — it does not prove the change applied. Wiring these to the id-based adapter would manufacture a verification claim that is not true.
26 matched only via a {vendor}.get_file_metadata fallback in the heuristic, which produced nonsense pairings such as slack.post_message -> slack.get_file_metadata. Not wireable.
47 have only a LIST sibling, which needs a scan pattern rather than this adapter.
164 have no registered read at all.
corrections_to_previous_revision.consequence: Coverage stays at 21.7%. Going higher needs a field-assert verification mode (compare the requested value against the read-back value), which is a new mode rather than a new declaration.

remaining_accepted_async.honest_caveat: 'No read sibling registered' means Gravitre does not register one. It is NOT evidence the vendor API cannot confirm the write. The per-vendor determination Phase 3.3 asks for has NOT been done for these 164.

status.3_1_read_back_for_every_supported_action: PARTIAL — the mechanism is built and now proven against a live vendor, and 75 inert declarations execute. But coverage is 21.7%, and every remaining action needs either a field-assert mode, a list-scan mode, or vendor-by-vendor investigation.
status.3_2_honest_lower_confidence_labelling: PARTIAL — backend projection and the shared outcome component carry three states and it is mutation-proven, but the user-visible result is UNVERIFIED at the deployed tip; the outcome card only renders behind auth. Handed to Cesar for a screenshot.
status.3_3_final_coverage_number_and_per_action: PARTIAL — real coverage number established (0.8% -> 21.7%) and the remainder categorised with reasons, but per-vendor capability for the 164 is not established.
